what: **Read end to end for the first time**, at **both** bands — parents and declarant — for work-list rows 35 and 86. Three acts of this volume were already cited in households; **the volume itself had never been read.**
got:
**NOTHING NEW, AND THAT IS THE RESULT.** Three Falco in the year and this archive already had all three.

**Act 30, 11 March 1824 — CLEMENTE FALCO**, to **GIUSEPPE FALCO, forty-eight, MASSARO**, and **ANTONIA DI GUIDA, forty**, of strada Camellara. **Act 31, 25 March 1824 — GIUSEPPE NUNZIO FALCO**, to **VINCENZO FALCO, thirty-three, contadino**, and **ANDREANA CRISCI, twenty-seven**. **Act 73, 18 June 1824 — GIUSEPPA CIOFFI**, to **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, twenty-seven, of strada CAMELLARA**, and **MARIA FALCO, twenty-five**, born at half past three in her father's own house, witnessed by **TOMASO SPOSITO, forty-six, of strada Camellara**, and **ANTONIO BERNARDO, forty-seven, *negoziante*, of strada Terra Murata**.

**Both Falco fathers declared their own children**, and both left pages say «*e da lui dichiarante*» — **so a parents-band sweep of 1824 would have seen an Antonia di Guida and an Andreana Crisci and no Falco at all.** The year is an argument for the second band even where it produces nothing.

## THE TAVOLA IS BLOCKED — BY THE SAME PAPER SLIP AS 1823

The 1824 *tavola alfabetica annuale* is on the right-hand page of image **154**, and **an archivist's card reading «THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY» lies across it.** Nothing of it can be read. **That is now two consecutive years — 1823 and 1824 — whose index is lost behind the same card**, which is why both have to be read act by act. The closing certificate, on the facing page, is signed 31 December 1824: «*di fogli scritti num. CENTOQUARANTANOVE, contenente atti num. CENTOQUARANTANOVE*».

## AND IT SETTLED A NAME THE CONTACT SHEET HAD GOT WRONG

At tile size image **120** reads «**ANDREANA CRISCI**, twenty-four» — which would have been a third woman of generation three's wife's name. **Magnified, the word is ANDREANA COSSI**: the C runs straight to an o, with no r shoulder and no i between them. She is the wife of **ANIELLO LOFFREDA**, and the 1826 *tavola* writes her the same way, in one hand, on the page that also writes «*Falco Vincenzo e CRISCI Andreana*». **Two independent readings, two years apart, agreeing.** *The sheet may produce a candidate, never a record.*

**Images 1–151 read; 152–153 blank; the Procuratore's certificate, dated S. Maria 1 March 1851, is image 155.**

**ACT 57, 4 MAY 1827 — MADDALENA FALCO**, born at eleven, to **GIUSEPPE FALCO, forty-five, COLONO**, and **ANTONIA DI GUIDO, forty**, of **strada CAMELLARA**. **This archive had her from the tavola alone and published the act number as 52. **ACT 69, 12 SEPTEMBER 1826 — ANGELANDREA FALCO**, to **VINCENZO FALCO, thirty-two**, and **ANDREANA CRISCI, twenty-eight**, of strada Camellara. **Already held**, and the citation is confirmed: the act opens on image **70 right** and its parents are on image **71 left**.

## AND A SECOND ANDREANA CRISCI, EIGHT LEAVES FROM THE FIRST

**Act 77, 16 October 1826**: **RAFFAELE**, to **GENNARO ESPOSITELLI, thirty-four, contadino of strada CAPODICONCA**, and **ANDREANA CRISCI, thirty-one**. **One register, one clerk's hand, two women of that name three years apart in stated age on two streets.** Both readings magnified; neither is in doubt. **Generation three's wife is identified in this archive by her husband and her street, and it is now documented that her name alone identifies nobody.**

## THE TAVOLA IS COMPLETE, AND IT AGREES

The 1826 *tavola alfabetica annuale* runs images **113–116** and is filled **through the whole alphabet** — the F group closes with *Fierro* and *Ferriello* and is followed by *Giglio*, *Guida*, *Liparulo* and *Loffreda* on the same page, so the page-break rule is satisfied. **It holds exactly one Falco birth: «69. Falco Angelandrea | Falco Vincenzo e Crisci Andreana | A dì 12 7bre 1826».** *It cannot answer for Falco MOTHERS, who are indexed under their husbands' surnames — which is how act 19 was missed for years.*

**A control pair, in one hand on one page**: «*Falco Vincenzo e **CRISCI** Andreana*» at act 69 and «*Loffreda Aniello e **COSSI** Andreana*» at act 8. **The C runs straight to the o in the second and takes an r shoulder in the first.** It settles the uncertain «Andreana Co—» of the 1822 register: **she is a COSSI, and she is not this line's Andreana Crisci.**

**No other Falco appears in the year at either band**, and no Falco presents a child. Images 1–108 read; 109–110 blank; the closing certificate is image 111.

Il presente volume contiene fogli NOVANTASETTE*». **It does not mean the year has ended.** The act numbering runs straight through it: image 102 is «*Num. d'ordine NOVANTASETTE … il dì VENTIQUATTRO del mese di OTTOBRE*». **A reader who stops at the title page loses October, November and December** — thirty-seven images and about thirty-six acts. **NO NUNZIATA — AND THE RE-READ FOUND WHAT THE FIRST PASS STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT.** Act 71, **8 August 1831**: **ANTONIA**, born at four in the morning on **strada Camellara** to **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, thirty-six, contadino**, and **MARIA FALCO, thirty-five**, baptised at Sant'Andrea the same day. **The declarant here is the father, a CIOFFI. A sweep of the declarant line sees no Falco in this act at all** — the Falco is the mother, three lines over on the facing leaf. That is the whole argument for the parents band, demonstrated on the one volume that had been done the other way.

**And the surname is plain in this hand**: *C-i-o-ff-i*, with the **i between the C and the o** that a *Cossi* does not have. **A third act confirming the 1825 correction.**

**She is the second Antonia**; the first died 20 June 1823. The household also buried a Mariantonia in 1828 and another on **3 December 1832** — which **may be this child at sixteen months**, and is **not claimed**.

## SWEPT A THIRD TIME BY MISTAKE — AND THE MISTAKE IS THE USEFUL PART, 21 September 2026

**This volume was swept again at the declarant band, and it should not have been.** Work-list row 85 listed 1831 among the years «still owed a second band». **It was not owed one: this row says in its own first sentence that the declarant line was the FIRST pass.** A hundred images were read for a third time.

**The reading stands and is recorded as a null**: images 1–98, **no Falco declarant**, and the year is carried by three midwives — **ROSA DELLA SELVA, seventy-nine**, **CATERINA RUGGIERO, seventy-three**, and **GELSOMINA RUGGIERO, fifty-two** — who between them present most of it. **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, thirty-six**, appears at image 73, which is act 71, Maria Falco's child, exactly as recorded above.

**Why it happened, and what was done about it.** `tools/staleness_report.py` exists to print precisely this pair — an open row asking for a year the coverage page records as read. **It printed nothing**, because its trigger words did not include «*still owed*», and «*remaining*» is not «*remains*». **A missing trigger word reads exactly like a clean report.** The tool has been widened and now finds it.

what: The Arienzo DEATH register of 1865 — the last volume in the series

SO HIS DEATH IS 1866 OR LATER, in the post-Unification Stato civile italiano this archive has never located for Arienzo. The same now holds for GIUSEPPE FALCO of Antonia di Guida, alive November 1849 and in no volume since. WHAT 1865 DOES HOLD: «e MATTEO FALCO di anni cinquantanove» as a DECLARANT in December — the second Matteo Falco, alive at about fifty-nine; and ANGELO MAJONE, 56, declaring in October — Pasqua Falco's first husband alive nine years after their wedding. A NAMESAKE CAUTION: act at image 68 buries a MARIA CARFORA at Arienzo on 24 October 1865. She is NOT generation seven's grandmother, who is of Forchia and bore children from 1883. THIRTEEN FALCO MARRIAGES were found and all are published, with five more Falco reached through the parents’ column. NO FALCO MARRIED AT ARIENZO in 1809, 1810, 1811, 1812, 1815 (bar Luigi of the Sebastiano house), 1816, 1817, 1820, 1821, 1822, 1823, 1824, 1826, 1827, 1830, 1831, 1833, 1835, 1837, 1838, 1841, 1843, 1844 or 1849. THE ONE RECORD THIS SWEEP SET OUT TO FIND AND DID NOT: the marriage of MARIA FALCO to FRANCESCO CIOFFI (this entry read COSSI until 15 September; the surname is CIOFFI, corrected from the 1825 register at full resolution, and the sweep was run on the BRIDE so the reading is unaffected). The likely answer is that THE ARIENZO CIVIL REGISTERS BEGIN IN 1809 and this marriage is older than they are — which would require her stated age of twenty-five in 1824 to be wrong by roughly eight years, a margin this register reaches routinely. src: The National Archives (UK), Discovery — discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk, 17 September 2026. The catalogue over TNA's own holdings at Kew plus some 2,500 other British archives. Every surname in this archive searched.
what: Falco, Zampiello, Annecchino, Arricale, Carfora, Crisci, Morgillo, Rivetti — and the three towns, Arienzo, Forchia, Arpaia
got:
**A CLEAN NIL FOR THE FAMILY, AND ONE RECORD ABOUT THE TOWN.**

**ZAMPIELLO 0 · ANNECCHINO 0 · ARRICALE 0 · CARFORA 0 · MORGILLO 0 · RIVETTI 0 · CRISCI 1 · FORCHIA 0 · ARPAIA 0.**

**FALCO returns 86, and not one of them can be this family.** They are British records of people who happened to bear the name: **eighteen WO service records** of British soldiers (service numbers, dates of birth 1903–1925); **twenty-one BT records** of merchant seamen registered at UK ports — «*R360597 FALCO J 11/10/1926 LONDON*», «*R542406 FALCO A 16/08/1917 SANTIAGO, CHILE*»; **twelve HO files**, mostly naturalisation certificates of Italians resident in Britain, the nearest being **Luigi Falco, born 17 July 1894 at SAVIANO**; a company dissolved in 1995; a lawsuit of 1515; and a Lake Como steamer. **«Falco Arienzo» returns 0. «Falco Caserta» returns 0.**

**This family has no British generation, and the catalogue confirms it rather than merely failing to contradict it.** The path is Arienzo → Forchia → Arpaia → Naples → Brisbane, and nobody on it registered as an alien, served the Crown, or signed on at a British port.

**BUT ONE FILE NAMES THE TOWN, AND IT IS WORTH ORDERING.** **WO 32/22147**, 1–31 March 1945: «*Special Investigation Branch investigation: alleged murder of Herron FG, Private, 1583838, Argyle and Sutherland Highlanders **by two Italian civilians at ARIENZO, Italy, 11 March 1945***». Open since 25 August 2017, held at Kew, **not digitised**. A British military police file about a killing in this family's town, five months before the war ended, which would name the accused and its witnesses. **It is a lead about Arienzo, not about the Falco, and it is recorded as that.**

src: Arienzo, «Registro degli atti diversi» — ANTENATI, 45 volumes, `an_ua14064`–`an_ua14106` plus `an_ua57637`–`57638`. The register of births at sea, recognitions, adoptions, PEOPLE WHO DIED AWAY FROM THEIR OWN HOME, and stillbirths. Read end to end, 17–20 September 2026.
what: FALCO and DI GUIDA — and in particular the deaths of ANTONIA DI GUIDA, alive 2 February 1845, and GIUSEPPE FALCO of Antonia di Guida, alive 26 November 1849
got:
**NO FALCO IN ANY OF THE FORTY-FIVE VOLUMES, AND NO DI GUIDA.** Every act from **1845 to 1865** is read and its dead are named — the whole window either person could fall in. Four acts in the series remain unnamed, all **before 1845**, so neither can be among them.

**When an Arienzo person died elsewhere, the comune where they died drew the act and sent a certified copy home, and Arienzo copied it in whole** — age, trade, street, both parents, whether they were dead, surviving children with their ages. So this was the one instrument that could hold a death the town never recorded. **It does not hold theirs.**

**What it does hold is about thirty-five deaths away from home, and they map where an Arienzo labourer went and did not come back from**: the **Ospedale degli Incurabili** at Naples (5), **Sant'Agostino degli Scalzi** at Aversa (3), the **Real Stabilimento de' Matti** and its women's side at Aversa (6), **Acerra** (3), **Caserta** (2), **Airola** (2), a masseria in the **Nola** district, **Montesarchio**, **Santa Maria Maggiore**, the **Ospedale della Trinità** — and once, **LIPARI**.

**PASQUALE PORRINO**, 52, a labourer born at Arienzo, died **31 October 1864 in the hospital of the DOMICILIATI COATTI on Lipari** — internal exile. **CARLO BALLETTA**, soldier of the **1st Dragoons**, died in the Ospedale della Trinità on 3 March 1855, his colonel writing to ask the sindaco to tell his family to collect **one ducat and thirty-five grana**, the price of his kit. **ANGELO IMBIMBO**, 60, died in the Aversa madhouse on 30 November 1855 — and **FRANCESCO IMBIMBO, «figlio d'Angelo»**, died in the **same asylum** on 4 November 1844. **Father and son, eleven years apart.**

**TWO CAUTIONS FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING.** The holdings query `localita=Arienzo` matches **several comuni** — Corpo d'Arienzo, **San Felice d'Arienzo**, **San Casale di Arienzo** — and the printed title page gives the CIRCONDARIO at the top, which is the district, not the town. **Read the comune from each volume's own title page.** And **from 1856 the clerk leaves the printed act heading blank and writes only the body**, so a sweep of the heading band reports «no acts» for a volume holding five.
